Prealgebra · Lesson 6.3

Variables on Both Sides

Solve this lesson →All lessons

In 6.2 the unknown sat on one side and the plain numbers on the other. Real situations are not always so tidy, and the same unknown can show up on both sides at once. Picture two scooter apps, one costing 2m+52m+5 and the other 3m3m. They cost the same when 2m+5=3m2m+5=3m, which has mm on both pans. You cannot isolate the variable while copies sit on each side, so the one new move is to subtract a variable term from both sides until the unknown is on one side only. Everything after that is the same work you did in 6.2.

Problem
A locker rental costs 7x+27x+2 and a bike rental costs 4x+174x+17, each over the same number of days xx, and today they came out equal, so 7x+2=4x+177x+2=4x+17. The new idea is that the balance rule lets you take the same term off both pans, and that term can be a variable. Subtract 4x4x from both sides to clear the xx off the right, then solve the one-sided equation. Solve 7x+2=4x+177x+2=4x+17 and type the value of xx.
Show a hint
  • Both sides carry an xx term. Subtract the smaller one, 4x4x, from each side so the variable survives on only one side.
  • After subtracting 4x4x you get 3x+2=173x+2=17. Now it is an ordinary two-step equation, subtract 2 then divide by 3.
Show the full solution
Subtract 4x4x from both sides. On the left 7x−4x=3x7x−4x=3x, and the right loses its xx term, leaving 3x+2=173x+2=17. Subtract 2 to get 3x=153x=15, then divide by 3 for x=5x=5. Both sides come out to 37, so 55​. Taking the same variable term off both pans is legal for the same reason taking off the same number is, the scale stays level.
Key idea
Gather the variable to one side. When the unknown shows up on both sides, the one new move is to collect every variable term onto a single side. The balance principle still applies, so adding or subtracting the same variable term on both sides keeps the equation true, exactly as it did with plain numbers. Once the variable sits on only one side, you are back to the one-sided equations from 6.2 and you finish the same way.
Problem
When the bigger pile of variables is on the right, a little planning avoids negatives. In 9+3x=7x+19+3x=7x+1, subtracting 7x7x would leave a negative xx term, so instead subtract the smaller variable term, 3x3x, from both sides so the survivor stays positive. Solve 9+3x=7x+19+3x=7x+1 and type the value of xx.
Show a hint
  • Compare the two variable terms, 3x3x and 7x7x. Subtract the smaller, 3x3x, from both sides to keep the remaining xx term positive.
  • After subtracting 3x3x you get 9=4x+19=4x+1. Subtract 1, then divide by 4.
Show the full solution
The variable terms are 3x3x and 7x7x. Subtract the smaller, 3x3x, from both sides so the survivor stays positive. The left becomes 99 and the right becomes 4x+14x+1, giving 9=4x+19=4x+1. Subtract 1 from both sides to get 8=4x8=4x, then divide by 4 to get x=2x=2. A quick check, the original left is 9+3(2)=159+3(2)=15 and the right is 7(2)+1=157(2)+1=15, so 22​.
Problem
Before moving anything across, tidy each side on its own. The left side of 5x+4−2x=x+125x+4−2x=x+12 has like terms hiding in it, so combine them first, then gather the variable onto one side. Solve 5x+4−2x=x+125x+4−2x=x+12 and type the value of xx.
Show a hint
  • The left side is not in simplest form. Combine 5x5x and −2x−2x into 3x3x, so the equation reads 3x+4=x+123x+4=x+12.
  • Now subtract xx from both sides to get 2x+4=122x+4=12, then finish with the usual two steps.
Show the full solution
Combine the like terms on the left, 5x−2x=3x5x−2x=3x, so the equation is 3x+4=x+123x+4=x+12. Subtract xx from both sides to get 2x+4=122x+4=12, subtract 4 to get 2x=82x=8, then divide by 2 for x=4x=4. Both sides come out to 16, so 44​. Tidying each side on its own first keeps the gathering step from getting messy.
Problem
A group can hide the variable until you distribute. In 2(3x−4)=4x+62(3x−4)=4x+6, expand the left side with the distributive property from 6.1, then collect the variable on one side. Solve 2(3x−4)=4x+62(3x−4)=4x+6 and type the value of xx.
Show a hint
  • Distribute the 2 across the group first. 2(3x−4)2(3x−4) becomes 6x−86x−8, so the equation is 6x−8=4x+66x−8=4x+6.
  • Subtract 4x4x from both sides to get 2x−8=62x−8=6, then add 8 and divide by 2.
Show the full solution
Distribute the 2 on the left, 2(3x−4)=6x−82(3x−4)=6x−8, so the equation becomes 6x−8=4x+66x−8=4x+6. Gather the variable by subtracting 4x4x from both sides, leaving 2x−8=62x−8=6. Add 8 to both sides to get 2x=142x=14, then divide by 2 to get x=7x=7. Check, the left is 2(3⋅7−4)=2(17)=342(3⋅7−4)=2(17)=34 and the right is 4(7)+6=344(7)+6=34, so 77​.
Key idea
The full procedure. First simplify each side by distributing and combining like terms. Next gather all the variable terms onto one side and the plain numbers onto the other, moving the smaller variable term so the one left behind stays positive. Then isolate the variable the way you did in 6.2, and finish by checking your answer in the original equation. This procedure solves every linear equation in this course.
Fun fact
About 1,700 years ago Diophantus of Alexandria used shorthand symbols for unknowns. He discarded any puzzle whose answer came out negative, calling such results absurd.
Problem
Nothing says the meeting value has to be a whole number. Solve 8x−3=3x+48x−3=3x+4, gathering the variable onto one side, and let the answer be a fraction if that is where it lands. Type xx as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Subtract 3x3x from both sides to get 5x−3=45x−3=4.
  • Add 3 to get 5x=75x=7, then divide both sides by 5. The answer is a fraction, so leave it in lowest terms.
Show the full solution
Subtract 3x3x from both sides to get 5x−3=45x−3=4. Add 3 to get 5x=75x=7, then divide by 5 for x=75x=57​, which is already lowest terms since 7 and 5 share no common factor. Both sides come out to 415541​, so 7/57/5​. A fraction answer is an ordinary result here, nothing needs rounding or fixing.
Problem
When a fraction sits in the equation, clear it first. In x3+4=x−23x​+4=x−2, multiply every term on both sides by 33 to wipe out the denominator, then solve the both-sides equation that remains. Solve x3+4=x−23x​+4=x−2 and type the value of xx.
Show a hint
  • Multiply every term on both sides by 3 to clear the denominator. x33x​ becomes xx, the 4 becomes 12, and the right side x−2x−2 becomes 3x−63x−6.
  • Now solve x+12=3x−6x+12=3x−6. Subtract xx, then finish.
Show the full solution
Clear the fraction by multiplying every term on both sides by 3. The left x3+43x​+4 becomes x+12x+12, and the right x−2x−2 becomes 3x−63x−6, so the equation is x+12=3x−6x+12=3x−6. Subtract xx from both sides to get 12=2x−612=2x−6, add 6 to get 18=2x18=2x, then divide by 2 to get x=9x=9. Check in the original, the left is 93+4=3+4=739​+4=3+4=7 and the right is 9−2=79−2=7, so 99​.
Problem
Try to solve 6x+5=6x−26x+5=6x−2. Gather the variable terms by subtracting 6x6x from both sides and watch what remains. How many solutions does this equation have? Type the single number.
Show a hint
  • Subtract 6x6x from both sides and watch the variable disappear entirely.
  • You are left with 5=−25=−2, which is never true. An equation that reduces to a false statement has no solution, so the count is 0.
Show the full solution
Gather the variable by subtracting 6x6x from both sides. Every xx vanishes, and you are left with 5=−25=−2. That statement is false, and no value of xx can ever make 6x+56x+5 equal 6x−26x−2, since the two sides always differ by 7. So the equation has no solution, a count of 00​.
Problem
Now try 3(2x+4)=6x+123(2x+4)=6x+12. Distribute the left side, gather the variable, and notice what is left. To feel the result, test three values, x=0x=0, x=7x=7, and x=20x=20. How many of those three are solutions? Type the single count.
Show a hint
  • Distribute the 3 on the left. 3(2x+4)3(2x+4) becomes 6x+126x+12, which is exactly the right side.
  • Since both sides are identical, every value of xx is a solution, so all three test values work. Count them.
Show the full solution
Distribute the left side, 3(2x+4)=6x+123(2x+4)=6x+12, which is precisely the right side. Gathering the variable by subtracting 6x6x leaves 12=1212=12, a statement that is always true. That means every value of xx is a solution, so the equation has infinitely many. In particular all three test values x=0x=0, x=7x=7, and x=20x=20 work, which is 33​ of the three. The equation is really just two ways of writing the same expression, the equivalent expressions you met in 6.1.
Key idea
Special cases. Sometimes the variable terms cancel completely when you gather them, leaving a statement with no variable at all. If that statement is true, like 6=66=6, every number is a solution, so the equation has infinitely many solutions. If it is false, like 5=−25=−2, no number works, so the equation has no solution.
Problem
A shop compares two presses over tt hours. The old press prints 3(2t+5)3(2t+5) pages and the new one prints 4t+274t+27, and at one hour count they match. Distribute the left side, gather the variable, and find it. Solve 3(2t+5)=4t+273(2t+5)=4t+27 and type the value of tt.
Show a hint
  • Distribute the 3 first. 3(2t+5)3(2t+5) becomes 6t+156t+15, so the equation is 6t+15=4t+276t+15=4t+27.
  • Subtract 4t4t from both sides to get 2t+15=272t+15=27, then subtract 15 and divide by 2.
Show the full solution
Distribute the left side, 3(2t+5)=6t+153(2t+5)=6t+15, so the equation is 6t+15=4t+276t+15=4t+27. Gather the variable by subtracting 4t4t from both sides, leaving 2t+15=272t+15=27. Subtract 15 to get 2t=122t=12, then divide by 2 to get t=6t=6. Check, the old press gives 3(2⋅6+5)=3(17)=513(2⋅6+5)=3(17)=51 and the new gives 4(6)+27=514(6)+27=51, so 66​.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Solve 9x=5x+129x=5x+12 and type the value of xx.
Show the solution
Subtract 5x5x from both sides, 9x−5x=4x9x−5x=4x, leaving 4x=124x=12. Divide both sides by 4 to get x=3x=3. Check, the left is 9(3)=279(3)=27 and the right is 5(3)+12=275(3)+12=27, so 33​.
Practice
Solve 7y+4=2y+247y+4=2y+24 and type the value of yy.
Show the solution
Subtract 2y2y from both sides to get 5y+4=245y+4=24. Subtract 4 to get 5y=205y=20, then divide by 5 to get y=4y=4. Check, the left is 7(4)+4=327(4)+4=32 and the right is 2(4)+24=322(4)+24=32, so 44​.
Practice
First combine like terms on the left, then gather the variable. Solve 7t+2−3t=t+177t+2−3t=t+17 and type the value of tt.
Show the solution
Combine the like terms on the left, 7t−3t=4t7t−3t=4t, so the equation is 4t+2=t+174t+2=t+17. Subtract tt from both sides to get 3t+2=173t+2=17, subtract 2 to get 3t=153t=15, then divide by 3 to get t=5t=5. Check, the left is 7(5)+2−3(5)=227(5)+2−3(5)=22 and the right is 5+17=225+17=22, so 55​.
Practice
Distribute the left side first, then gather the variable. Solve 6(w−2)=3w+66(w−2)=3w+6 and type the value of ww.
Show the solution
Distribute the left side, 6(w−2)=6w−126(w−2)=6w−12, so the equation is 6w−12=3w+66w−12=3w+6. Subtract 3w3w from both sides to get 3w−12=63w−12=6. Add 12 to get 3w=183w=18, then divide by 3 to get w=6w=6. Check, the left is 6(6−2)=246(6−2)=24 and the right is 3(6)+6=243(6)+6=24, so 66​.
Practice
Solve 7x+1=2x+97x+1=2x+9 and type xx as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Subtract 2x2x from both sides to get 5x+1=95x+1=9. Subtract 1 to get 5x=85x=8, then divide by 5 to get x=85x=58​. Since 8 and 5 share no common factor, it is in lowest terms. Check, the left is 7⋅85+1=565+55=6157⋅58​+1=556​+55​=561​ and the right is 2⋅85+9=165+455=6152⋅58​+9=516​+545​=561​, so 8/58/5​.
Practice
Clear the denominator first by multiplying every term by 22. Solve y2+5=y−12y​+5=y−1 and type the value of yy.
Show the solution
Multiply every term on both sides by 2 to clear the fraction. The left y2+52y​+5 becomes y+10y+10, and the right y−1y−1 becomes 2y−22y−2, so the equation is y+10=2y−2y+10=2y−2. Subtract yy from both sides to get 10=y−210=y−2, then add 2 to get y=12y=12. Check, the left is 122+5=6+5=11212​+5=6+5=11 and the right is 12−1=1112−1=11, so 1212​.
Practice
Gather the variable in 3x−4=3x+53x−4=3x+5 by subtracting 3x3x from both sides, then read what remains. How many solutions does it have? Type the single number.
Show the solution
Subtract 3x3x from both sides. The variable cancels completely and leaves −4=5−4=5, a false statement. The two sides always differ by 9, so no value of xx can ever make them equal. The equation has no solution, a count of 00​.
Practice
Distribute the left side of 4(x+2)=4x+84(x+2)=4x+8 and compare it with the right. Test x=1x=1, x=9x=9, and x=50x=50. How many of the three are solutions? Type the count.
Show the solution
Distribute the left side, 4(x+2)=4x+84(x+2)=4x+8, which matches the right side exactly. Gathering the variable leaves 8=88=8, always true, so every value of xx is a solution and there are infinitely many. All three test values x=1x=1, x=9x=9, and x=50x=50 work, which is 33​ of the three.
Practice
Two gyms charge by the month. Over mm months gym A costs 7m+187m+18 and gym B costs 9m9m. Find the month count where they cost the same. Solve 7m+18=9m7m+18=9m and type the value of mm.
Show the solution
Subtract 7m7m from both sides to gather the variable on the right, leaving 18=2m18=2m. Divide both sides by 2 to get m=9m=9. Check, gym A costs 7(9)+18=817(9)+18=81 and gym B costs 9(9)=819(9)=81, so they match at 99​ months.
